title: tune NCCL stream priorities and scheduling to improve overlap for tensor-parallel
author: Aisha Kumar
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel workloads are increasingly exposed to NCCL collectives contention where suboptimal stream ordering and kernel/comm scheduling reduce achievable overlap between communication and compute. This PR tunes NCCL stream priorities, introduces explicit scheduling for collective streams vs compute streams, and exposes runtime knobs so deployments can trade latency vs throughput. It also includes small microkernel scheduling hints to reduce kernel-stream synchronization points. Approach: 1) add a StreamManager that creates two prioritized CUDA stream pools (high-prio for collectives, default for compute) and pins NCCL ops to the high-prio pool; 2) modify the TP scheduler to submit local compute kernels on default streams while coordinating collective launches on high-prio streams with lightweight host-side fences; 3) add a runtime config (redwood.runtime.tp_streaming.priority_scheduling = true/false) and a per-model override; 4) add a KV-cache warmup path that opportunistically issues cache fetches on lower-priority streams to avoid blocking critical compute; 5) add unit and integration tests plus a benchmark harness job to measure overlap benefits. Changes include both C++ runtime and Python orchestration glue to ensure compatibility with existing reclaimer/worker logic. Testing and results: ran the benchmark-lab tp-8x-a100 job and internal on-prem 8xA100-40GB cluster with a 70B-like GPT model. Synthetic throughput (tokens/s) improved by ~12% on steady-state streaming workloads; 95th percentile token generation latency reduced by ~18% for seq_len=2048; end-to-end inference CPU overhead increased slightly (~+3%) due to extra bookkeeping. Benchmarks also include stress runs that confirmed no NCCL deadlocks and faster recovery during transient load spikes. Rollout: feature gated off by default; enabled in canary for dedicated customers with GPU families supporting stream priorities (A100/V100); config exposed in console and via API. Rollback plan: disable priority scheduling runtime flag and revert to single-stream fallback; documented known limitations (older drivers may not respect priorities, see linked notes). Related: links to ENG-9843, ENG-10012 and previous PRs tuning NCCL overlap.

performance_summary: Steady-state throughput: +12% tokens/sec on tp streaming workloads (8xA100, 70B-like model)
95th percentile token generation latency: -18% for seq_len=2048
KV-cache warmup reduced cold-start token latency by ~9% in warm-up scenario
CPU overhead: +3% due to stream bookkeeping
No NCCL deadlocks observed in 72h stress run; transient spike recovery improved
release_notes: Runtime: Add priority-based NCCL stream scheduling for tensor-parallel workloads. Enables improved overlap of comm and compute resulting in lower tail latency and higher throughput for multi-GPU models. Feature is off by default and behind redwood.runtime.tp_streaming.priority_scheduling. See docs/perf/tp-nccl-streams.md for details and compatibility notes.
notes: Compatibility: stream priorities only effective on GPU drivers and architectures that honor CUDA stream priority semantics (tested on A100 with driver >= 470.XX). If users see regressions they should toggle the runtime flag. Follow-up work scheduled in ENG-10012 to add richer telemetry and canary automation.
